scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether deleting my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch was right or wrong. Let me start by going through the situation step by step. First, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom were on a trip. I brought my Switch because I have a long commute to school, and I wanted something to do during the train ride. My stepbrother really liked playing on it, so I made a new profile for him so he wouldn't mess up my saves. That seemed like a good idea at the time because it kept things organized and prevented any accidental deletions or changes to my games. After that week, I went back to school. I noticed that every time I started a game or went to the eShop, I had to click on my profile each time. It was a minor inconvenience, but it started to annoy me. So, I decided to delete his profile to make things simpler for myself. I didn't think much about it because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit, so I didn't expect him to use it again. Then, during Thanksgiving, I brought my Switch again for the train ride. My stepbrother picked it up to play, and when he saw that his Zelda save was gone, he started freaking out. He came into the kitchen where I was talking with my dad, and he was really upset, even crying a little. Now he's shut himself in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete the profile because he knew my stepbrother was enjoying playing on it. I didn't think it was a big deal because I usually don't bring the Switch over, but clearly, it affected him a lot. So, was it right or wrong to delete his profile? Let me think about the different aspects. On one hand, the Switch is my property, so I have the right to manage the profiles on it. I created the profile to help him, but when it became inconvenient for me, I deleted it. That seems a bit selfish because I didn't consider how much he might care about his progress in the games. On the other hand, I was trying to maintain my own space and convenience. I didn't want to deal with the hassle of switching profiles every time I used the Switch. Plus, I didn't expect him to use it again when I brought it over for Thanksgiving. But the fact that he was so upset shows that he did care about his profile and the time he spent playing. My dad's reaction also indicates that it was seen as mean, which makes me think that maybe I should have handled it differently. I guess the main issue here is communication. I didn't talk to my stepbrother about deleting his profile. If I had explained why I was doing it and maybe offered to help him save his progress elsewhere, he might not have been so upset. Instead, I just deleted it without any warning, which probably made him feel like I didn't care about his feelings. Another thing to consider is the impact on our relationship. My stepbrother is upset, and now he's shut in his room. This could create tension between us, especially during Thanksgiving, which is supposed to be a time for family bonding. My dad's disapproval also adds to the negative outcome. So, reflecting on this, I think deleting the profile without discussing it with my stepbrother was wrong. It was a lack of consideration for his feelings and a failure to communicate effectively. I should have found a way to address the inconvenience without causing emotional harm. Maybe I could have moved his profile to a different system or found another solution that respected both our needs. In the future, I should remember to talk things through and consider how my actions might affect others, especially family members. It's important to balance my own needs with the feelings of those around me to maintain a positive relationship.
